title: Mode-I center-crack LEFM extraction
purpose: Verify that the public finite-element workflow and the DOLFINx interaction-domain adapter recover crack-tip stress intensity and energy release rate from a solved displacement field.
physics: two-dimensional plane-stress isotropic linear elasticity with a traction-free straight center crack under remote tension

source.title: Infinite-plate center-crack solution
source.reference: K_I = sigma sqrt(pi a), K_II = 0, J = K_I^2 / E for plane stress

execution.structural_api: Study -> Model -> model.step -> DOLFINx interaction-domain lowering -> StressIntensityReport -> verification
execution.evidence: A P2 displacement solve on a conforming split mesh is sampled independently over three annular domains. The measured K_I, K_II and J are compared with the analytical infinite-plate reference; a separate exact Williams-field test verifies mixed-mode plane-stress and plane-strain normalization.

acceptance: The solved finite-plate K_I differs from sigma sqrt(pi a) by less than 3%.
The solved finite-plate J differs from K_I^2 / E by less than 5%.
The relative variation across three extraction domains is less than 2%.
The spurious K_II magnitude is less than 3% of reference K_I.
Invalid tensor shape, unsupported dimension, invalid radii and empty integration domains fail explicitly.
observables: K_I and K_II for each extraction radius
limitations: The executable split-mesh fixture is serial and intended for verification rather than general crack meshing.

The current interaction-domain formula assumes a straight crack, homogeneous isotropic LEFM, quasi-static equilibrium, and no body force, thermal eigenstrain or applied crack-face traction in the extraction domain.
The finite plate is compared with an infinite-plate formula; its remaining finite-boundary and piecewise-linear geometry effects are included in the measured error.
This benchmark verifies a stationary predefined crack, not crack growth.
